Joulewise Advisory Private Limited has carried out an independent Energy Yield Assessment (EYA) of the proposed Hybrid Power Project (Solar + Wind + BESS) consisting of the following project configuration and site, for supply of Firm and Dispatchable RE power under the NHPC 1,200 MW FDRE Tranche-II tender (200 MW part capacity):

The entire 200 MW grid connectivity is shared across the Solar, Wind and BESS components, being the Contracted Capacity under the NHPC FDRE Tranche-II RfS.
Only the generation meeting the Contracted Capacity is considered for FDRE compliance; energy beyond the evacuation limit is either stored in the BESS or curtailed.
There is no Non-Participating / merchant plant component in this project configuration; the entire capacity operates under the FDRE PPA.

6. HYBRID EYA SUMMARY
6.1. Methodology

The study is carried out to understand the revenue potential of the proposed project. A rule-based, day-ahead-aware dispatch simulation is used to model the hybrid plant’s 15-minute generation, BESS charge/discharge behaviour and settlement against the tender’s Firm and Dispatchable RE power supply conditions. Main components of the assessment are as follows:
A. Objective – Maximize Revenue Generating Energy
Revenue generating energy = Energy Supplied under PPA − 1.5 × Energy Shortfall under PPA + 1.0 × Energy Surplus
Note:
Since each unit of energy shortfall is penalized at 1.5 times the tariff, the weightage considered for energy shortfall is as per the PPA terms.
In order to prioritize PPA supply over the surplus, the surplus is given a lower weightage.
B. Constraints

Annual basis: (a) Minimum CUF under the PPA – any supply below the minimum CUF will be penalized as per PPA terms; (b) Maximum CUF under the PPA – any supply above the maximum CUF will not be purchased under the PPA.
Monthly basis: Minimum monthly availability during the peak hours – any supply below the minimum monthly availability during peak hours will be penalized as per PPA terms.
Hourly/15-min basis: (a) Supply under PPA cannot be more than the PPA capacity in any time block; (b) Total evacuation, i.e. sum of supply and surplus, cannot be higher than the evacuation capacity.
C. Inputs

First-year 15-minute generation profiles of Solar at P50, P75 and P90 (synthesized from the PVsyst monthly output, scaled to 275 MWac). Using a deration factor of 0.4%/year, hourly/15-min generation profiles are calculated for the rest of the project life.

First-year 15-minute generation profiles of Wind at P50, P75 and P90 (interpolated from the source hourly resource data, scaled to 44.1 MW), degraded year-on-year at 0.20%/year over the 25-year PPA term.

Profile of BESS including initial capacity, charging and discharging rates, losses in percentage, depth of discharge, State-of-Health schedule for life of the battery, round trip energy schedule. BESS Usable Capacity (MWh) for each year = Nameplate Capacity (400 MWh) x State-of-Health (%) x Depth-of-Discharge (%); this year-specific usable capacity (not the flat nameplate value) is used as the operative energy limit in the dispatch simulation for that year, together with the corresponding year-specific Round-Trip Efficiency.

A flat Auxiliary Consumption of 1.5% per year is deducted from Gross Supply (Simultaneous Supply + ESS Supply) to arrive at Net Supply under the PPA, representing the hybrid plant’s own station power/parasitic load.
D. Assessment
Assessment is carried out at P50, P75 and P90. Energy generated by the solar and wind is distributed among the following components:
Simultaneous Supply – The energy supplied immediately to the buyer under the PPA is called Simultaneous Supply.

Supply to Energy Storage Solution (ESS) – A part of the energy generated is supplied to ESS to meet the demand when the generation is unable to meet the peak period demand. A part of this energy is lost due to internal transmission losses and energy conversion losses of the ESS. The rest is used for charging the ESS. The energy that ultimately charges the battery (i.e., after the losses) is termed as Energy for ESS Charging.

Surplus – The generated energy that is in excess to (i) Simultaneous Supply and Supply to ESS on an hourly basis within contracted capacity, and (ii) upper limit of supply allowed under PPA, is the surplus which is available for sale to other buyers.
Curtailment – The energy that cannot be evacuated due to the evacuation limit or stored in the ESS is called Curtailment.

Losses – Losses are the ESS Transmission Loss and ESS Conversion Loss. ESS Transmission Loss is the loss of energy due to transmission of AC power (i) from the generation busbar to the ESS and (ii) from the ESS to the Point of Injection. ESS Conversion Loss is the loss of energy due to (i) conversion AC to DC and (ii) conversion DC to AC and (iii) losses within the ESS.
The hybrid generation is the sum of the above five components.
Supply
Energy supply under the PPA has two components:
Simultaneous Supply – Explained under Generation and Utilization section above.
ESS Supply – Energy supplied by the ESS to meet the supply obligations under the PPA.
6.2. Supply Conditions and Revenue Components
The revenue generated from the proposed project is from three components:

Supply under the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). As per PPA, the proposed project should meet the following conditions: (a) Annual CUF of the proposed project should be between -15% and +10% of the declared CUF; (b) Monthly availability of the proposed plant should be 90% during the peak hours; (c) Tariff is common for both peak as well as non-peak hours.
Sale of surplus to other buyers. Surplus can be: (a) Unused generation over and above the PPA capacity on the hourly basis; (b) Unused generation over and above the annual CUF + 10% on annual basis.
Penalty for shortfall on the supply as per the PPA supply conditions. This component has a negative impact on the revenue. Penalty is calculated as 1.5 times the tariff for the shortfall energy.

Peak hours: 2 hours within 05:00-10:00 and 2 hours within 18:00-23:00 daily (4 hours total), as scheduled by the Buying Entity. This assessment adopts an illustrative schedule of 08:00-10:00 and 18:00-20:00 pending the actual notified schedule.
6.3. Hybrid Project Results

Considering the FDRE Tender requirement, permitted power evacuation capacity, BESS utilization, clipping analysis, generation profile and other technical details, a detailed Hybrid Generation analysis has been performed on different probability values of generation of both Wind and Solar energy.

For Hybridization, year-on-year degraded hourly generation profiles were used for both the Wind (0.20%/year) and Solar (0.40%/year) power plants over the 20-year assessment period, together with a year-specific BESS usable capacity (Nameplate x SoH x DoD) and Round-Trip Efficiency, and a flat 1.5%/year Auxiliary Consumption deduction.

Note: Wind energy generation was initially estimated at the 220 kV grid interconnection level, which inherently includes losses associated with transmission lines and power transformers. The generation was subsequently adjusted to the 33 kV level by excluding the transmission and transformer losses. In contrast, the solar generation was directly estimated at the 33 kV level. The solar energy available at the 33 kV level was then considered as the input for battery charging, and a rule-based dispatch approach was employed to determine the optimal battery charging and estimate the overall hybrid energy generation.

Note on methodology: (i) Solar 15-minute generation shape is synthetic (sunrise/sunset-based, inverter-capped), scaled to reproduce the PVsyst-reported monthly energy exactly; P75/P90 monthly shapes are derived by applying the uniform annual P75/P90-to-P50 ratio, as no monthly P75/P90 split was available from the source PVsyst report. (ii) Wind per-MW basis assumes 1 WTG = 3.15 MW; per-MW yield is scaled to the selected 44.1 MW capacity. (iii) Solar degradation of 0.4%/year and Wind degradation of 0.20%/year are applied year-on-year over the 20-year assessment. (iv) BESS: 400 MWh is the Nameplate Capacity; the Usable Capacity applied in the dispatch simulation for each year = Nameplate x SoH (%) x DoD (%), together with the corresponding year-specific Round-Trip Efficiency (84.64% in Year 1, degrading per the SoH schedule); SoH schedule assumes battery augmentation restoring 100% SoH in Year 11. (v) A flat Auxiliary Consumption of 1.5%/year is deducted from Gross Supply to arrive at Net Supply under the PPA. (vi) Monthly Peak Availability is assessed on an ENERGY-RATIO basis (Actual Peak-Hour Energy Supplied / Required Peak-Hour Energy per month) consistent with the RfS provision that shortfall is calculated at the end of each month.
